qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Valuable primary-airport slot portfolios at London Gatwick, Geneva, and Paris provide local frequency advantages, but short-haul aviation is structurally commoditized and shopped on OTAs. 10-year median ROIC is sub-7% (far below the 12% hurdle), with structural margin compression from volatile jet fuel, airport charges, and aggressive ULCC competition.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Reject – G3 Moat & Pricing). European low-cost passenger airline operating from primary airport slots. While Gatwick and Geneva slot portfolios offer local slot protection, easyJet's cost structure sits above ultra-low-cost peers (Ryanair/Wizz Air) while seats are commoditized. 10-year median ROIC is in the 5-7% range (failing the 12% hurdle), with zero durable pricing power over economic cycles.
qualitative.evidence: Over the last decade, easyJet's ROIC has averaged well below the cost of capital: 2023-2025 normalized ROIC recovered to only 4.5-8.6%, following severe pandemic losses (-10% to -12% in 2020-2021) and pre-COVID returns of 6-9% (2018-2019). High exposure to jet fuel price volatility, union wage inflation, and European passenger fare sensitivity destroys structural pricing power.
